- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially for short-term (1-7d) horizon.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00), leading to over-forecasting in 1-3d; apply dampening factor to next 3-5d.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10-30d horizon: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 15-30% in next 7d.
- Sentiment volatility >0.30 in 3d window correlates with forecast divergence; apply smoothing filter to reduce noise in 10-15d horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to misalign with true trend; align forecast to sentiment median over 5d window.
